Bihar Initiates Process to Remove Untrained Teachers Appointed After March 2015 Following Supreme Court Directive

01 Nov 2026, 08:13 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Careers Desk · Source: navbharattimes.indiatimes.com

Image: Navbharat Times · Source image rights not independently verified · Photo source · Cropped to 16:9 for the website

Key takeaways Overview of the Directive Following a recent Supreme Court directive and subsequent instructions from the education department, authorities in Bihar have initiated the process to review and potentially terminate the services of untrained government teachers appointed

Overview of the Directive

Following a recent Supreme Court directive and subsequent instructions from the education department, authorities in Bihar have initiated the process to review and potentially terminate the services of untrained government teachers appointed after March 31, 2015. The Primary Education Directorate in Bihar has instructed District Magistrates (DMs) and District Education Officers (DEOs) to compile lists of such teachers across districts.

According to reports from teacher associations and media sources, an estimated 35,000 untrained teachers appointed after the March 2015 cut-off date face job uncertainty in Bihar alone, though the exact figures are subject to official district-wise verification currently underway. For instance, reports indicate that over 500 such teachers have been identified in Muzaffarpur district alone.

Background and Legal Context

The development stems from enforcement of the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009, which mandates that school teachers possess formal training qualifications such as B.Ed or D.El.Ed. While initial rules permitted certain appointments under the Bihar Panchayat Elementary Teacher Rules 2012 with a requirement to complete training, the Supreme Court ruled that appointments made without mandatory academic and training qualifications after the March 31, 2015 cut-off date are invalid. Conversely, untrained teachers appointed prior to March 31, 2015, have reportedly been granted an extension to acquire D.El.Ed qualifications by August 31, 2028.

Impacted Teachers and Teacher Union Stance

  • Reported Claims from Teachers: Affected educators state they completed their D.El.Ed training through platforms like NIOS or IGNOU subsequent to joining, with some even clearing the 'Sakshamta Examination' to attain state employee status.
  • Union Demands: Teacher unity organizations have demanded a stay on the termination of teachers appointed after March 31, 2015, urging the withdrawal of departmental notifications and the filing of a review petition in the Supreme Court.

Notification and Application Details

  • Issuing Authority: Primary Education Directorate, Bihar / District Education Offices
  • Notification ID / Reference: Not specified in source (References include letter memo numbers such as 2853 dated October 1, 2026, and 351 dated March 25, 2015)
  • Posts: Government Primary Teachers (Untrained category appointments)
  • Eligibility: Not specified for new applications (Current notices pertain to service termination review)
  • Age Cut-off Date: Not specified
  • Vacancies: Approximately 35,000 reported statewide (subject to district verification)
  • Fees: Not specified
  • Application Dates: Not specified (Service termination and verification process ongoing)
  • Selection Stages: Document verification and district-wise list compilation
  • Result, Admit Card, and Answer Key Status: Not applicable

*Note: Official notices and application links were not verified in the source text. Stakeholders are advised to verify announcements directly through official Bihar education department portals.*
